newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA SETS FOREIGN INVESTMENT REPATRIATION NORMS.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA SETS FOREIGN INVESTMENT REPATRIATION NORMS.

text.p: Romania's central bank (BNR) said on Wednesday it approved long-awaited norms regulating repatriation in greenfield and portfolio foreign investment, a move expected to boost foreign confidence.

Under the new norms, non-residents acting as foreign investors are given access to the local foreign exchange market where they can submit spot or forward hard currency orders related to their investments in Romania.

The procedures follow a June government decree on portfolio deals allowing foreign investors to freely repatriate the initial investment and capital gains. A tax of up to 1.5 percent is applied to each portfolio deal.
To become effective the new norms have yet to be published in the country's Official Gazette.

Under the new norms hard currency buying and selling transactions would be recorded in a foreign investor's account and would be handled solely by commercial banks licensed to operate on the Romanian interbank market.
"Foreign investors will no longer encounter procedural hurdles," a BNR official told Reuters.
So far, Romania lacked clear norms on foreign investors' access to the market for repatriation.
Non-resident companies which do not have a foreign investor status are only allowed to sell foreign currency on the local interbank market, the BNR rules said.

Banks operating in Romania will monitor investors' deals, checking on the source of the inflows. Hard currency buying orders should be backed by documents showing that leu funds came from foreign investment transactions.
Romania has seen large foreign capital inflows in the past few months after the new centrist government pushed ahead with the market reforms stalled under the former ex-communists.
Foreigners turned bullish on Romanian equities and securities even before portfolio rules were adopted in June pushing up stock exchange and over-the-counter volumes.
